generalfeedback.text:
A vertex that is not a whole-number point is not an answer: test the whole-number points of R around it. Rounding \({@vd@}\) to \(({@rp[1]@}, {@rp[2]@})\) breaks a condition: \({@brkd@}\). Rounding a vertex can carry you outside R, so check every constraint.

Test the whole-number points near the vertex that satisfy both conditions and work out \(P = {@pp@}x + {@pq@}y\) at each. The best is \(x = {@bst[1]@}\), \(y = {@bst[2]@}\), with profit Ksh \({@thou(t)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: best whole-number plan

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (c) / Essential 1.4 (c): Given the optimal vertex of a feasible region, find the best whole-number plan near it by sampling, and its profit.

Core and Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 8, Section 2.3 of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: choosing the best whole-number combination rather than the corner of the region, with Kenyan contexts and new numbers.
